title: When You Lose Passion for the Work
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This short Admired Leadership piece addresses the leader or professional whose enthusiasm for a long-held role has quietly faded, without the person being burnt out. It first normalizes the experience, arguing that sustaining strong passion for the work over a long stretch is the exception rather than the rule and that the passion is only on temporary leave. Its central move is to reject simply grinding through the torpor in favor of starting a fire somewhere else: a hobby, a new skill, a charitable cause, or a new way of adding value at work. Because passion is contagious, the author argues, enthusiasm found in another arena tends to spill back into one's engagement with colleagues and the work within months. The piece closes with a fallback: if the work still feels unbearable, seek a new challenge, ideally inside the current workplace where one already has credibility and allies.
points: Waning enthusiasm after long service is framed as normal rather than as burnout or failure, which removes the shame that often keeps leaders stuck.
Instead of trying to rekindle passion for the work directly, the author recommends kindling it in another arena, on the premise that passion is contagious and spreads back into everything else.
The suggested outlets range from hobbies and languages to charitable causes and adding value at work in a way one never has before.

If renewed passion elsewhere does not restore engagement, the prescription is a new challenge, sought first within the current organization where one's credibility and supportive colleagues already exist.
quotes: After giving a role everything you’ve got for a lengthy time, passion for the work can sometimes wane. It’s not that you’re burnt out or endlessly tired, it’s just that the enthusiasm you had for the work has diminished to the point where you have noticed it. You don’t look forward to engaging with others nearly as much as you used to.

In actuality, maintaining a strong passion for the work over a long period of time is the exception, not the rule. It is completely within the bounds of normality to lose a step or two regarding your excitement about the work.

Instead of rekindling the fire for the work, start another fire somewhere else. Passion is contagious and discovering your enthusiasm in another arena will frequently increase your passion everywhere else, as well.

Move toward your excitement about a new endeavor and dig in. Let the newfound excitement wash over everything in the way you engage others. Within a few months, you’re likely to find your passion for the work returns with a fresh head of steam.

If after finding passion elsewhere you still find the work more unbearable than ever before, you need a new challenge. Try to find that new challenge in your current workplace, where everyone knows your skills and talents, where you have the runway of credibility and colleagues who want you to succeed.
